A.explanation: 100 Hz gives $\lambda = 3.4 \text{ m}$ so $L = \lambda/4$, the fundamental mode with node at closed end and antinode at open end.

B.explanation: 200 Hz gives $\lambda = 1.7 \text{ m}$ so $L = \lambda/2$, which is an even multiple of $\lambda/4$ and cannot satisfy node plus antinode conditions.

C.explanation: 300 Hz gives $\lambda \approx 1.13 \text{ m}$ so $L = 3\lambda/4$, the third harmonic of the closed pipe.

D.explanation: 500 Hz gives $\lambda = 0.68 \text{ m}$ so $L = 5\lambda/4$, the fifth harmonic of the closed pipe.

hints: Notice the pipe is $0.85 \text{ m}$ long, closed at one end with a node there and an antinode at the loudspeaker end.
Recall a closed pipe fits only odd numbers of quarter-wavelengths: $L = \lambda/4, 3\lambda/4, 5\lambda/4...$
Calculate $\lambda = v/f$ with $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for each frequency and test which length is not an odd multiple of $\lambda/4$.
walkthrough: Identify the boundary conditions: displacement node at the closed end and antinode at the open end where the loudspeaker is.
State the resonance condition for a closed pipe: $L = (2n-1)\lambda/4$ for $n = 1,2,3...$, so only odd multiples of a quarter-wavelength fit.
Find the fundamental frequency from $v = f\lambda$ with $\lambda_1 = 4L$: $f_1 = v/(4L) = 340/(4 \times 0.85) = 340/3.4 = 100 \text{ Hz}$.
Allowed frequencies are odd harmonics: $f = f_1, 3f_1, 5f_1... = 100 \text{ Hz}, 300 \text{ Hz}, 500 \text{ Hz}...$.
Check 200 Hz: $\lambda = v/f = 340/200 = 1.7 \text{ m}$, so $L/\lambda = 0.85/1.7 = 0.5 = 2/4$, an even multiple of $\lambda/4$ that cannot form node-antinode pattern.
Therefore 200 Hz would not produce a stationary wave. This is option B.
